indian_entity: Settled Muslim community on India's west coast (Saymur/Chaul)
chinese_source: Al-Masudi, Muruj al-Dhahab (completed 943, revised 956), reporting his Indian sojourn of c. 915-916
event: Masudi reports some 10,000 bayasira (locally born Muslims) at Saymur (Chaul, Konkan coast) with ordinary and Friday mosques, protected by the Hindu king — a settled, second-generation, mosque-building Muslim community under Hindu rule
firmness_reason: Eyewitness-grade traveller report, but the named town is Saymur on the Konkan coast, NOT Malabar proper; the figure of 10,000 is a traveller's round number
notes: Bounds the regional pattern: by c. 915 mosque-building Muslim settlement under Hindu kings is normal on the west coast north of Malabar. It does not attest Malabar itself, and Masudi tells no convert-king story.
references: Al-Masudi, Muruj al-Dhahab wa Ma'adin al-Jawahir (943/956)
